newsitem.title: UK: Frankfurt closes at peak, others end down.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt closes at peak, others end down.

text.p: German stocks closed at a record high on Wednesday but other European bourses finished in the minus column, dogged by worries over interest rates. On currency markets, the dollar was stronger in late European trading as dealers took an optimistic view of the outcome of a policy-making meeting of the U.S. central bank which started earlier on Wednesday.
In Frankfurt, floor trading extended its record-breaking rally and closed at a new peak, boosted by the strengthening dollar, which was seen as helping exports.
The DAX index of 30 leading shares reached an all-time trading high and then closed up 39.13 points at 2,773.43, eclipsing the record set only last Friday.

Computerised deals measured by the IBIS index broke the intra-day record set on Tuesday, climbing to 2778.83 points, a gain of 0.4 percent, as the dollar climbed decisively over the psychologically-important 1.50-mark level.

"The lights are all on green," said one trader as screen-based deals continued to climb despite a poor start in Wall Street when the Producer Price Index came in stronger than expected, stoking inflation worries for some.
Frankfurt bourse dealings, particularly in export-oriented chemicals and car shares, had been held back by the weak dollar, which had been trading at a two-month low near 1.49 marks.

The dollar got a boost after the Tuesday IBIS close on comments by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer that the U.S. currency was once again on its way higher and that he always welcomed the dollar being at its correct level.
In London, Europe's biggest bourse, stocks edged lower as investors, depressed by worries over interest rates, digested the opening in Wall Street, where Dow Industrials fell 0.26 percent.
Amid the uncertainty, investors were also focusing attention on the rate-setting U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting.

But most analysts expected the Fed would hold rates steady as the see-saw U.S. economy was seen as settling down. This view. which has fuelled New York's recent bull run, would be greeted with relief by global equity markets. But in Britain's case, investors were still jittery. A steeper-than-expected drop in British unemployment and strong unit wage costs revived concerns about inflationary pressures, further depressing markets.
"It all looked a bit gloomy after the jobs data hit gilts and futures and we never really recovered from that," one dealer said, noting that Wall Street's dull opening also hit sentiment.

In Paris, stocks ended down 0.6 percent after being in the doldrums all day. A large state sale of shares in Elf adding to pressures. Analysts said Wall Street's dip accentuated the consolidation after Tuesday's year high on the Paris bourse.
On currency markets, the dollar strengthened against the mark and the yen, buoyed up by traders' optimism over the FOMC meeting.

"You almost have this Goldilocks scenario in the U.S. with solid sustainable growth and no inflation. Certainly in the near term I don't see that threatened," said Stuart Weatherby, economist at Panmure Gordon.
Analysts said the U.S. currency was also supported by comments on Tuesday from Bundesbank officials, including Tietmeyer, supporting a firmer dollar.

"German industrial production figures have been weaker than expected. In light of that, the Buba is not going to want a strong Deutsche mark...I wouldn't rule out further cuts in repo rates further out," said Weatherby.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was at 1.5051 marks and 111.42 yen in late European trading, compared with 1.5015 marks and 111.38 yen on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 7.4 points lower at 3,926.9.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished down 11.94 at 2,217.19.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 39.13 at 2,773.43.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold ended at $384.05 an ounce, up from $381.75 at the London close on Tuesday. Silver closed at $4.92, up five cents.
